name: Jean Grey
summary: Marvel's most famous comeback act. Jean Grey, founding X-Man and powerful telepath and telekinetic, is forever bound to the cosmic Phoenix Force and its habit of bringing her back.
origin: Jean Grey has died and come back so many times that X-Men fans treat her funerals as temporary. She began, though, as Marvel Girl, the only woman in the original lineup of The X-Men #1 in 1963, a teenage mutant who could move objects with her mind. Telepathy came later, along with astral projection and empathy, and in 1976 Chris Claremont bonded her to the cosmic Phoenix Force. The Dark Phoenix Saga that followed, where the Phoenix turns murderous and Jean dies, is still the benchmark for X-Men storytelling. Her 1986 return started a long tradition of Jean coming back, and the Phoenix keeps following her.
powers: Phoenix Force: cosmic fire and control of matter

storyline.title: Marvel Girl
storyline.beat: Jean Grey joins the original X-Men as Marvel Girl, the team's only female member, using telekinesis and later telepathy.

storyline.title: Rising from the crash
storyline.beat: After piloting a shuttle through a solar storm, Jean seems to emerge as the far more powerful Phoenix.

storyline.title: Too much power
storyline.beat: Corrupted by her power, Jean destroys a star and an inhabited planet. Facing judgment, she ends her own life on the Moon to protect everyone.

storyline.title: She was never there
storyline.beat: Jean is found alive in a cocoon under Jamaica Bay. The Phoenix had copied her, so Jean returns to found X-Factor with the original X-Men.

storyline.title: Dying again
storyline.beat: In Grant Morrison's run, Jean is killed during an attack by Magneto, while her marriage to Scott falls apart.

storyline.title: Back for good
storyline.beat: Phoenix Resurrection brings the adult Jean back to life, and she soon leads her own X-Men team.

gossip.text: Claremont and Byrne first planned for Jean to survive the Dark Phoenix Saga. Editor-in-chief Jim Shooter said wiping out a populated planet needed a harsher ending, so she died.
Jean Grey herself became Dark Phoenix.
gossip.truth: The 1986 retcon says the Phoenix Force copied Jean while she lay in a cocoon. The real Jean was asleep for the whole saga.

gossip.text: Kurt Busiek is credited with the idea that brought Jean back in 1986.
She was the only woman in the original X-Men lineup.
Rachel Summers, from an alternate future, is Jean and Scott's daughter.

quiz.q: What was Jean Grey's first codename?
quiz.why: She debuted as Marvel Girl in 1963.

quiz.q: Where does the Dark Phoenix Saga end?
quiz.why: Jean's final stand happens on the Moon.
She married Scott Summers in X-Men #30.

timeline.title: Marvel Girl
timeline.note: The X-Men #1 introduces Jean as the team's only woman, a telekinetic who later reveals her telepathy.

timeline.title: Rising as Phoenix
timeline.note: X-Men #101 has Jean emerge from a crashed shuttle as the Phoenix, bursting with cosmic power.

timeline.title: The Dark Phoenix Saga
timeline.note: Uncanny X-Men #137 ends the classic saga with Jean choosing death on the moon over losing control again.

timeline.title: Alive in a cocoon
timeline.note: Fantastic Four #286 reveals the real Jean was sealed away all along, opening the door to her return.

timeline.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
timeline.note: The Fox Kids cartoon adapts both Phoenix stories for TV.

timeline.title: Finally marrying Scott
timeline.note: X-Men #30 finally gives Jean and Scott their wedding.

timeline.title: Famke Janssen in X-Men
timeline.note: Bryan Singer's X-Men casts Famke Janssen as Jean, a doctor caught between Scott and Logan.

timeline.title: Phoenix Resurrection
timeline.note: A five-issue series brings Jean back for good after her 2004 death in New X-Men.
